title: Python stdlib unittest (floor 3.11, CI 3.11 + 3.x on three OSes)

rules.rule: Write tests against the 3.11 API only: no TestCase.assertStartsWith/assertEndsWith/assertHasAttr/assertIsSubclass (3.14), no TemporaryDirectory(delete=...) (3.12), no --durations in the CI command (3.12).
rules.why: The 3.x leg of the CI matrix passes and the 3.11 leg fails with AttributeError/TypeError (or an unknown-option usage error), and a developer on a new Python never sees it locally.

rules.rule: Do not use the removed TestCase aliases (assertEquals, assertNotEquals, assertRegexpMatches, assertRaisesRegexp, assert_, failUnless*, failIf*, assertDictContainsSubset) or the module functions unittest.makeSuite/findTestCases/getTestCaseNames; use the canonical assert* names and TestLoader methods.
rules.why: The aliases were removed in 3.12 and the module functions in 3.13: the test errors with AttributeError on the 3.x leg while the 3.11 leg stays green.
where: tests/*.py (none in use today; grep clean)

rules.rule: In every test module import tests._support (or `from tests import _support`) before any `stackfoundry` import, and keep tests/ a regular package with __init__.py run as `discover -s tests -t .`.
rules.why: tests/_support.py puts plugins/stackfoundry/scripts on sys.path at import time. A module that imports stackfoundry first works under full discovery only because an earlier module (sorted by name) already ran _support, and fails with ModuleNotFoundError when run alone or reordered. A test subfolder without __init__.py is not discovered (namespace start dirs unsupported on 3.11; subdirectories without __init__.py are not searched on 3.14), so its tests silently never run.
where: tests/test_globs.py and tests/test_frontmatter.py (`from tests import _support  # noqa: F401`)

rules.rule: Pass timeout= to every subprocess.run in a test (the repo uses 120 s in tests/_support.py git and run_cli).
rules.why: timeout defaults to None: a child that blocks (git waiting for an editor or credential, a shell reading stdin) hangs the CI job until the runner's own limit with no test named. With timeout, run() kills the child and raises TimeoutExpired, which fails the one test.

rules.rule: Give an explicit encoding="utf-8" with every text=True subprocess call and every read_text/write_text/open in tests; for raw-bytes protocol tests (the guard) pass bytes and no text mode.
rules.why: On 3.11 to 3.14 text mode defaults to the locale encoding (cp1252 and similar on the windows-latest leg): the Cyrillic and other non-ASCII paths these tests use come back mangled or raise UnicodeDecodeError. UTF-8 becomes the default only in 3.15.
rules.repoConvention: Already followed everywhere in tests/ (grep of read_text/write_text/subprocess.run).
rules.until: 3.15 makes UTF-8 the default; keep explicit while the floor is below 3.15

rules.rule: Run the CLI under test as the hook does: through tests/_support.run_cli (sys.executable -I cli.py), not by calling a different interpreter or omitting -I.
rules.why: -I drops the script directory and user site-packages from sys.path and ignores PYTHON* variables; without it a developer's environment can make a test pass that fails under the real launcher, or the reverse.

rules.rule: Loop over data with self.subTest(...) and assert the collection is non-empty before the loop (as FixtureProfileTests does with assertTrue(overlays)).
rules.why: Without subTest the first failing item hides the rest; without the non-empty assertion a glob that matches nothing (a renamed folder) makes the test pass vacuously while checking nothing.

rules.rule: Release resources with a context manager, addCleanup or enterContext (3.11+), not tearDown alone.
rules.why: If setUp raises, tearDown does not run but registered cleanups do: temp repos and processes leak and later tests on the same box see stale state.

rules.rule: Guard tests that need an external tool with @unittest.skipUnless(<probe>, "<reason>") at the class or method, and check the -v CI log on each OS that they actually run there.
rules.why: A skip is reported as success: a probe that is false on a CI runner means the test never runs anywhere. Since the 3.12 fix an all-skipped run no longer exits 5, so nothing turns red.
rules.repoConvention: Skip with a reason when git or sh is missing (tests/_support.py HAS_GIT).

rules.rule: Do not rely on the exit status to catch an empty discovery on the 3.11 leg; the 3.x leg is the one that exits 5 when no test ran.
rules.why: Exit code 5 for 'no tests run' exists since 3.12; on 3.11 a broken discovery (bad -s/-t, missing __init__.py) reports OK with exit 0.

bugCategories.name: api-newer-than-floor

bugCategories.failure: AttributeError/TypeError on the Python 3.11 CI leg; green locally on a newer Python.

bugCategories.name: vacuous-loop-assertion

bugCategories.lookFor: A test module that imports stackfoundry (or anything under plugins/stackfoundry/scripts) before tests._support, or relies on sys.path state set by another module.

testing.layers: unittest proves the CLI modules in-process (stackfoundry.* functions) and end to end through a subprocess that runs the CLI isolated as the hook does (tests/_support.run_cli); fixture tests run the survey on fixtures/<name> and assert the stacks their EXPECTED.md promises.
harness: tests/_support.py (TempRepo, write, git, run_cli, targets_json, HAS_GIT, ROOT, PLUGIN, CLI, LAUNCHER)
commands: python -m unittest tests.test_guard -v   (one module; must pass alone)
python -m unittest discover -s tests -t . -k <substring>   (-k since 3.7; substring or fnmatch pattern on the full test id)
python -m unittest discover -s tests -t . --durations 10   (3.12+ only; not on the 3.11 CI leg)
python -W error::DeprecationWarning -m unittest discover -s tests -t .   (turn deprecations into errors; unittest.main otherwise shows them with the 'default' filter)
coverage run -m unittest discover -s tests -t . && coverage report   (coverage.py 7.17.2, Python 3.11+; dev-only, see questions)
testing.shuffle: The stdlib has no shuffle: discovery sorts module paths and method names, so the order is fixed. Stdlib-only option: a small runner script that calls unittest.TestLoader().discover('tests', top_level_dir='.'), flattens the suite, shuffles it with random.Random(seed) where seed comes from an argument or is printed, and runs it with unittest.TextTestRunner. The docs warn interleaving reruns setUpClass/setUpModule; this suite uses neither, so it is safe today. Third-party option: pytest + pytest-randomly (Python 3.11 to 3.15; prints --randomly-seed=N, reuse with --randomly-seed=N or last) runs these TestCase classes (subTest supported since pytest 9.0, load_tests not supported). Both are open questions: the runner script is new repo code, pytest is a dev-only dependency.
testing.mutation: No mutation tool in use for this suite; not researched in this run.
traps: Most CLI behaviour is tested through run_cli subprocesses, so plain `coverage run` under-reports: subprocess measurement needs `[run] patch = subprocess` plus `parallel` and `coverage combine`. The coverage docs do not say whether this survives the -I flag run_cli passes; verify before trusting the numbers.
The 3.11 leg exits 0 on an empty discovery; only the 3.x leg exits 5.
Shared fixtures (setUpClass/setUpModule) run more than once if the order is ever shuffled; keep per-test setup.

Cleanup of TemporaryDirectory can raise PermissionError on Windows when a file in it is still open (for example a child process still running); close or wait for children before leaving the with block.
Returning a value from a test method is deprecated since 3.11 (a test written as a helper that returns a result).

security.note: CVE-2023-6597: tempfile.TemporaryDirectory dereferenced symlinks during cleanup on permission errors (3.11.8 and prior). CI's "3.11" resolves to the latest 3.11 patch; a local 3.11 older than that is affected. The suite creates no symlinks today; a test that adds them should run on a patched interpreter. Offline exposure, low weight.

lockStep: The floor in scripts/stackfoundry.sh, the "3.11" CI matrix entry and the 'Python 3.11+' statement in .claude/CLAUDE.md move together; raising the floor unlocks the 3.12+ APIs listed in the rules.
